name: Desk Terminal, Wired
tagline: One cased terminal wired into the family's desk: Home's glass says 'Give Vera something to plan.', a lit lead runs to Coming up's NOW lamp, every dated list leads with one day numeral, and each band has exactly one light.
concept: The same cased terminal stands at the left of the desk on every page (6px case, 2px bezel), and a lit patch lead runs from a socket on the case to Coming up's white-hot NOW lamp. Home's glass shows the scrollback: 'Vera, Friday 2 October', Next up in inverse VT323 beside a small radar, then 'Give Vera something to plan.' in bone. Only 'plan.' is white-hot, followed by the site's one block cursor. The page is built on a few rules. Every dated list leads with a day numeral, and the next plan's numeral carries one lit mark wherever it appears. Every list hangs from a steel rail whose stops are lamps. Each band has exactly one light. The tube light glows at full strength on the glass, the dial, the lead and the lamps; the desk around it stays calm and in grounded colours.
companions: Wheat (#d8c38a), now 3px: the cap over every band, the left edge of Finish setting up, and the cap of the phone's closing foot. Grounded kind inks, used only in the ring and the kind word: clay for restaurants, straw for activities, moss for outings, dusk for trips and day trips, heather for shows, events and other, clay-orange for seasonal. The ways to start take the ink of where they usually land: dusk for Plans, straw for To do, heather for Ideas. Heather is also the dashed open stop 'Add an idea'. Dusk: the month word beside each day numeral. Dim: the weekday under it. Bone: the family's words and unlit numerals. Steel: rails and stops, now drawn through Lately added's rings. Graphite with a phosphor LED and underline marks 'here'; the steel slab is gone. Pewter: upcoming and off lamps. Sage: hover and a ticked box. Muted rose (#c39aa8): wishes. Amber: only late and 'needs a look'. Denim: links.
decisions: Built from the design's own build.py: the themed base, then palette.css, with spaces outside strings stripped. The sheet is 180.8k of the 200k budget, after deleting the Status contents scroll-spy block.

Title: put back 'Give Vera something to plan.', the line the cross lessons give to Desk alone. 'to plan.' is held on one line, so the lit word never sits alone. The lit run is color-mix(screen 30%, #fff) under the E1 halo (0 0 .06em #fff, 0 0 .35em screen, 0 0 1em rgb(109 255 156/.45)).

The cursor is the site's only one. It blinks 8 times, then holds. Its off phase falls to a 50% afterglow instead of disappearing (its own keyframe, afterglow-blink), so a still or a glance always finds it. That fixed it vanishing on home-phone. The wordmark's caret is removed from base.html, so no other page shows a cursor.

One day mark: Coming up's NOW-row numeral and every future plan day in the month share one rule: --screen ink, a tight E1 halo, and a 1px phosphor underline (text-decoration, so it sits under the figures themselves). Past plan days get a steel underbar. Rows 2-4 stay bone. Beside each numeral, the month is Plex Sans 500 at 0.75rem in dusk and the weekday is in dim.

The dial's day numerals are 22 units (about 20px on the 15rem glass). The sweep wedge's leading edge now stops 12deg short of its target, not the 4 the brief named: at 4deg the wedge's width still touched the '4' label.

Two label kinds, as one rule. A label names a control or a group (label, .keys-name, .plate-name): sentence case, Plex Sans 500, --fs-small, --label, no tracking. A column head over figures (.data th, month th, colheads, eyebrows) stays Plex Mono caps, tracked, as the machine's own. The deck's 'From' is now the rule, not an exception.

Lately added: the steel rail is now drawn through both columns (row position:relative, rings above the line). The right column ends in the rail's open stop, a dashed heather ring with 'Add an idea' and 'or tell Vera one', so the columns are 3 and 3 and the head drops its duplicate '+ Add an idea'.

Phone order with no CSS reordering: the case's two-line foot (Ready, then the wishes) is drawn twice from one macro: in the case on a wide screen, and as .phone-foot closing the page on a phone. One copy is always display:none, so a screen reader meets it once. Ways to start are 44px rows on the phone. Coming up's first row now sits at 831px on a 390x844 phone, inside the first screen (it was about 2 screens down).
The 'Where I am' toggle's accessible name is now aria-label 'Send where I am'. The visible caption is aria-hidden, 0.8125rem on desktop, and hidden on the phone, so the From row is one 44px line.
Bar: the desktop current key keeps its graphite face and its 12px phosphor underline. The 4px dot under it now appears only on the phone tab bar, which has no face.
Settings and the form: the Ready chip sits flush right at the panel's edge (margin-left:auto in a head row capped at the panel's 62rem), the same on every folded page.
Status: removed the scroll-driven 'in view' latch that lit every band on screen (two at once at the top). The Contents plate now has no false 'here' state.
Month chips: clamped to 2 lines with the full title in a title attribute. The clamp's link padding is zeroed so no third line bleeds under the time, and the time keeps its own line.
Home's green share went from 65.3% to 60.3% with no lost light. Wheat caps and the setup edge went to 3px, and Send's side padding is a little tighter.
title: *plan.*: 'Give Vera *plan.*' is wrong; exactly: "Give Vera something to *plan.*". It names who hears you, and 'something' takes in plans, reminders, ideas and wishes, which is FamilyDB's job: the family hands things to Vera and she plans them.
measures: Final full render: 0 hard checks failed, 1 guideline missed. ink_on_bg 12.49, brand_on_bg 15.18, glow, screenGlow and topGlow 1.0. Home: green share 60.3% (was 65.3%), hue entropy 0.549, coloured share 2.36%, other-colour neon share 5.8%. Ideas: green 74.2%, entropy 0.396 (the map glass). Chat: 72.7%. Status: 42.8%. Smallest text is 12px (Home's month word 'Oct'). No sideways scroll. The one WARN is 'page's words unchanged' (plans, 44.3% of words differ), which is expected for this design. Phone: Coming up's first row at y=831 on 390x844, To do at 1360, Lately added at 1738, the closing foot at 2139. Tab on Home goes from the bar to the textarea, then the select, toggle, mic and Send. The harness lists the toggle as 'input: 1' because it reads the value; its accessible name is 'Send where I am'.
strengths: It is clearly the same machine as Patched: the cased terminal, the patch lead into the white-hot NOW lamp, the rails whose stops are controls, and the four tubes.
The day numeral is now one mark: the lit '4' in Coming up's NOW row, the dial's lit ticks and the month's plan days use the same ink, halo and underbar.
One label system across Plans, To do, Ideas, Status, Chat and the forms. Mono caps are kept only for column heads.
The phone puts the next plan inside the first screen without reordering anything. The foot closes the page instead of standing between the box and Coming up.
Lately added has two balanced columns, each on a drawn steel rail, ending in an open stop that invites the next idea. It has one lit lamp ('newest').
The glass keeps the lineage's title and its heat. The cursor never disappears in a still, and it is the only one on the site.
weaknesses: The month chips still share one dusk edge. The month route gives entries no idea kind, and I can only change templates, so the kind graft stops at the grid.
The 2-line clamp cuts plan names in the month ('Mount St. Helens d…', 'Nutcracker at the…'). The full name is only a hover title away.
Home's green share is 60.3%, just over the 60% target. Ideas (74%) and Chat (73%) stay greener because their glasses are large.
Status no longer shows which band you are reading. The double latch is gone, but no single 'here' replaced it.
The phone's closing foot is inset a few pixels from the full-bleed bands above it.
On desktop the toggle's 'Where I am' caption still makes the From row taller than the keys beside it.
revisions: Title restored to 'Give Vera something to plan.' with the lit run on 'plan.'. The halo is set to the critic's exact E1 values over the hot core.
The cursor now has an afterglow blink (8 blinks, then holds, never invisible) and shows on home-phone. The wordmark caret is removed everywhere, so the cursor is Home's alone.

Phone: the case foot (Ready plus wishes) closes the page through a second copy of the same macro, one copy always hidden. Ways to start are 44px with tighter padding, the empty #where line is hidden, and the 'Where I am' caption is hidden. Coming up row one is at 831px.
Toggle: aria-label 'Send where I am', the visible caption is aria-hidden, and it is 0.8125rem on desktop.

Numeral law: the NOW row's numeral takes the month's lit mark (screen, tight halo, 1px underbar), now one shared rule. Month and weekday are Plex 500 0.75rem, the month in dusk and the weekday in dim. The dial's day numerals went up to 22 units. The sweep wedge stops 12deg short (declined the brief's 4deg because it still touched the '4' label).
Labels: one rule for label, .keys-name and .plate-name (sentence case, Plex Sans 500, --fs-small, --label, untracked). Column heads stay mono caps.

Lately added: the steel rails are drawn through the rings. The right column is balanced 3 and 3 with an 'Add an idea' open stop, and the head's duplicate link is gone. I did not add idea #5: the route sends only these ideas, and an invented row would misstate the data.
Bar: the 4px dot is dropped on desktop and kept on the phone tab bar.
Form and Settings: the Ready chip sits flush right at the panel edge on both.
Status: removed the scroll-driven double 'here' highlight.
Month: chips clamped to 2 lines (with a title attribute), and the time stays on its own line.

Declined: per-kind left edges on month chips. The month template gets no kind for a plan (agenda entries have none) and the route cannot be changed, so guessing a kind from title words would be a guess dressed as data.
Green share brought from 65.3% to 60.3% with 3px wheat caps and setup edge and a tighter Send. I did not dim the primary or the glass to get under 60%.
crit: HOME glass title (templates/home.html line 54, .ask-question): the designer changed the title to 'Anything for Vera to plan?'. That is a question form the cross lessons retire, and it gives up the title the lessons assign to Desk alone ('Give Vera something to plan.', its 7.95 setting). The lit run has also lost its heat: 'plan?' reads as pale bone next to the parent's white-hot 'plan.'. Restore 'Give Vera something to plan.' with the lit run on 'plan.'. Strengthen .ask-question .glow (sheet.css ~3123) back to the E1 two-layer halo over a hot core: color-mix(in srgb,var(--screen) 30%,#fff), text-shadow 0 0 .06em #fff, 0 0 .35em var(--screen), 0 0 1em rgb(109 255 156/.45). The caret is missing on home-phone: the .crt-cursor after the label must not be hidden or wrapped away at 390px, since it is the one cursor on the site.

HOME-PHONE order: at 390×844 Coming up's first row falls about 2 screens down, because the whole .terminal-foot (Ready plus wishes) and the three 48px ways-to-start rows sit between the deck and Coming up. At <=640px, move .terminal-foot after Lately added (grid order, or put the wishes line at the very end per the brief's phone order), and drop the ways-to-start rows to 44px with tighter top padding, so Coming up starts within 1.5 screens. Check the deck too: the bare 'Where I am' caption under the toggle makes the From row two lines tall. Put it in the toggle's aria-label on the phone, so the row is one 44px line.

THE NUMERAL LAW is not one mark yet. On Home, Coming up's numerals (4, 9, 17, 24) are unlit light-weight bone, while the dial and the month light the same figures in --screen with an underbar. Give the NOW row's numeral (the '4' where the lead lands) the same lit mark as the dial and month (--screen, 1px phosphor underbar, tight E1 halo), and leave rows 2-4 bone. The stacked 'Oct / Sun' VT323 beside each numeral is about 11px and grey. Set it in Plex 500 at 0.75rem: the month in --dusk (the brief says month names are dusk) and the weekday in --dim. On Plans, the dial's day numerals still read about 14px; set .dial-day at 1rem or more as the brief says. The sweep wedge still touches the lit '4' tick at 12 o'clock; stop it 4deg short.

LABELS have two systems. The deck's 'From' is now sentence-case Plex 500, but every other control label is still tracked uppercase mono: VIEW and MONTH (Plans), SHOW and SEARCH (To do), KIND, FOR and STATUS (Ideas), ON THIS PAGE (Status), CONVERSATIONS (Chat), and TITLE, KIND, SUGGESTED BY and DESCRIPTION on the form. Make one rule in the label class used by .terminal and form labels: sentence case, Plex Sans 500, --fs-small, --label, no letter-spacing. Then the From change is a law, not an exception.

LATELY ADDED balance and rails: the right column holds only Cannon Beach and 'Something to eat', so it ends one row short of the left, the same ragged foot judges marked before. Split 3/3 by letting 'Something to eat' (the restaurants group) close the right column under a 'See them' link and adding idea #5 (Mount St. Helens, dusk Day trip), or flow columns with column-fill:balance. The steel rails each column was meant to hang from are invisible; draw the 1px steel rail through the kind rings, as on the ways to start, so the band shares the desk's 'every list hangs from a rail' grammar.

PLANS month chips: every chip uses one dusk left edge, so the kind graft stops at the grid. Pass the plan's idea kind into plans_month.html (a data-kind on .plan-chip, from plan.idea.kind or the idea lookup the list view already uses) and map it to --clay/--straw/--moss/--dusk/--heather like the Ideas list. Long names wrap to 3 lines ('Mount St. Helens day trip'). Cap chip titles at 2 lines with line-clamp and keep the time on its own VT323 line.

WORDMARK and HERE marks: the block cursor after 'FamilyDB' shows on Home and Status but not on Plans, To do, Ideas, Chat, Settings or the form. The brief says the cursor appears only on Home's glass, so remove it from the wordmark everywhere (or keep it on every page, but not on two). In the bar, the current key now carries a graphite face, a 2px phosphor underline and a 4px dot under it: three marks for one state. Drop the dot under the bar key (keep it only on the phone's tab bar, where there is no graphite face). The terminal keys' right-hand LED already is their dot, so their underline can stay.

FORM and SETTINGS heads: on the New idea form the 'Ready' chip floats at about x 760, detached from both the subtitle and the right edge of the 1024px panel. Seat it right after the subtitle as on Settings, or flush right to the panel's edge, and do the same on every form. On Status the contents rail highlights rows 1 and 2 both (two steel-tinted rows), which reads as two 'here' states; keep one. Fix the toggle's accessible name: 'Send Where I am' (the health text shows it, and the focus order reads it as 'input: 1'). Give it aria-label 'Send where I am' and take the visible caption out of the name, and raise .loc-word from 12px to at least 0.8125rem.

firstDraft.name: Desk Terminal, Wired
firstDraft.concept: This is the same cased terminal at the left of every page, now wired into the family's desk. A lit lead runs from a socket on the case to Coming up's NOW lamp, and a bright pulse runs along it from the socket once the tube has warmed up. Every dated list leads with one day numeral, which is also used on the Plans dial and in the month grid. Every list hangs from a rail whose stops are lamps, with the square tick box beside each one. Each band has exactly one light. The phosphor glows at full strength on the glass, the dial, the lead and the lamps, while the desk around it stays calm and in grounded colours.

name: Quote Board, Lit
tagline: An evening count board set as open typeset columns: a figure that counts is printed in its section ink, and a figure that is live is lit phosphor with the tube's halo.
concept: Quote Board, Posted with the boxes off, and every figure under one law: a figure that counts is ink, and a figure that is live is light. Every list and plate hangs from a 2px cap rule in its section's ink, with 1px seams between columns, on every page. On each page exactly one figure glows with the original tube's layered halo, and the green screens around it draw real data. It feels like a calm evening trading desk where the light falls only on what is happening now.
companions: Grounded inks, each with one job. Steel-cyan is Plans: Coming up's cap, its count, the hop months and now the hop day numerals, since a date is printed in its section's ink. Status's Keys bank and Keys column are steel-cyan too. Wheat is To do's cap, on Home and as the rule the To do register hangs from. To do's figure is bone, so amber means late and nothing else. Heather is Ideas: Lately added's cap and figure, the cap of the Ideas register and the new-idea form, and Status's Links bank and Connected to column. Clay is people: the Family figure on the ticker, the family's names and initials (now on a faint clay tile) in chat, and, new, the Answers count and Who answers column on Status, which used to be bright phosphor. Pink is the wishes figures. Steel is the setup rings, the checkbox wells, the Settings index and the cap over each Settings group, and the edge of Vera's older chat lines. Amber is only caution: 'was due' words with their 2px row edge, the '3 late' link, the setup figure and lamp, 'to finish', 'needs a look' and the edge of the Settings card that needs a look. The cobalt wash stays in the greeting's far corner. Bone is for headings and for every count that is not live.
decisions: Built in place on the first draft (variants/x14b-quote-cross/). The six-rule header stays, with rule 6 as the law: 'A figure that counts is ink; a figure that is live is light.' The changes sit in the LIT FIGURES layer and a new LIT FIGURES, REVISED layer at the foot of sheet.css.

One light a page, kept strictly. Home: the next stop's day '4' on the L026 tiny tube under Coming up. Plans list: the same tube. Month: the next plan's day numeral, lit on the grid. Status: its '6 working'. Chat: the time of her newest reply. To do: its NOW lamp. Home's quote-screen '2' is now screen text: the screen's own phosphor with a 1px core and a 12px bloom, and no 34px halo, so it no longer outshines the lit figure. Status's Answers count '3' went from bright phosphor to clay, its bank's ink.

Home's quote screen now hangs from the eyebrow row ('Vera | FRIDAY 2 OCTOBER') down to the foot of the box. On desktop .welcome-words is display:contents, so the speaker and the box take column 1, the screen spans rows 1-2 of column 2, and the ways to start run under both. The glass is filled with data, not stretched raster: the title, now 1.75rem, a 6.25rem '2 DAYS', a new dim 'THEN Fri 9 Mount St. Helens day trip' line (the plan after next, as a quote screen runs the next symbol), the four-week tape and 'All plans'.

Status's three lower plates (Who answers, Keys, Connected to) are typeset columns now. Each stands under a 2px cap in its bank's ink (clay, steel-cyan, heather) with 1px seams, and its heading icon takes the same ink. The banks beside the tube were unboxed in the same way, each with its own ink cap. 'What it has cost' hangs from a plain rule.

Status's foot: the tracked mono '30-DAY AVERAGE $0.04 a day 6 calls' row is gone, since the glass already says 'avg $0.04'. Its place under the banks went to real data: a dotted-leader register of what the month was spent on (kind of call ···· calls ···· $). The plate's foot is a sentence-case legend, '$1.26 in 30 days, 6 calls', with 'Change the limit', level with the tube's foot.

Settings index: the '0·1' to '0·9' indices are gone, here, in the side list and in the bar's menu. Each part's head is now label, dotted leader, arrow. The cards are open columns under one steel cap with 1px seams, and the icon wells are hairline only. The part that needs a look keeps a 2px amber edge. On a part's page, every group is unboxed under a 2px steel cap, and folded groups under a 1px rule.

To do's register and the Ideas register each drop their outer box and hang from a 2px cap in their section's ink (wheat, heather). Their column heads are sentence-case sans at 0.8125rem on both pages, not tracked mono caps on one of them. The new-idea form is an open sheet under a heather cap.

Month view: the next plan's cell carries the page's lit figure, its day numeral in VT323 at 2.1rem with the E1 halo, and its plan chip has a 2px phosphor left tick. Today's '2' stays a slate chip. The head legend now reads 'next Sun 4 Oct · 13:00', the same as Home's dates.
Dates drop the leading nought everywhere (the stamp macro): 'was due Thu 1 Oct', not '01 Oct'.

Chat head: the whole change line is Plex 500 at 0.9375rem, 'last 27 Sep · 19:53', with only '19:53' carrying .fig-live, so the line keeps one face and one x-height. Vera's older lines are edged in steel mixed into the rule grey (no green), and her older screens are desaturated to 35%, so the newest line's phosphor edge and afterglow stand alone.

Phone: the quote screen drops the Then line, its case padding is cut to 0.3rem, the tape is 2.9rem, and the figure is 3.2rem. main and html get 5.5rem of bottom scroll-padding and padding for the fixed tab bar. Coming up's cap and head now show above the bar at 390px.
title: *What should* / *Vera plan?* is set on two lines with the lit run 'plan?', question mark included, under E1 at full strength. Written: 'What should / Vera *plan?*'. It names who hears you, and 'plan' is FamilyDB's job: a weekend plan, a reminder, an idea kept for someday or a wish all become something Vera plans.
measures: The full render passes with 0 hard checks failed. The one guideline missed is the expected 'page's words unchanged' (plans, 48.1% of words differ). ink_on_bg 12.49, brand_on_bg 15.18. brand and screen are both exactly #6dff9c (L 0.897, C 0.186, h 151.4). Green share of saturated pixels: home 68.2%, ideas 62.2%, chat 70.9% (down from 74.9), status 56.0%. Hue entropy: home 0.49, ideas 0.42, chat 0.37, status about 0.46. Bright green per mille: home 5.5, status 0.8. Smallest text is 11.7px (a code line on General). No sideways scroll on any page. Every CIEDE2000 pair passes; the narrowest are sections/protan 5.5 and kinds/deutan 6.1. Sheet is 199,433 characters, under the 200,000 cap. No small targets were added: ticker segments, setup links and the quote-screen links keep 44px hit areas. Home's and Chat's green shares are still above the brief's ~55%. On Home almost all of the green is inside the greeting plate (the lit 'plan?' and its halo, the tube, Send). I measured that cutting the pool does not move the figure, so the rest of the motif was not dimmed to chase the number.
strengths: One law, held strictly: exactly one lit figure on every page (Home and Plans the next day on its tiny tube, the month's next cell, Status '6', Chat '19:53'), with every count in matte section ink. The quote screen's '2' was brought down to screen text, so it no longer competes.

The system now holds off Home. Status's banks and columns, the Settings index and groups, the To do and Ideas registers and the form all hang from 2px section-ink caps with 1px seams. The heads are label-leader-figure (or arrow), and column heads are sentence case everywhere.

The quote screen is real data from the eyebrow row down to the box's foot: next plan, its day and hour, a big '2 DAYS', the plan after it, and a four-week tick tape. No empty glass was made by stretching.
Status's ground beside the tube carries the figures behind the average (a dotted-leader register of spend by kind) instead of a repeated mono caps row. The plate's foot is level with the tube's.
The type system is tightened: one face per legend line (the chat head in Plex), no leading noughts in dates, the Settings numbering gone, and the same sentence-case column heads across registers.
Grounded colour has clear jobs. Clay took over Status's Answers from phosphor, steel-cyan dates the hop rows, and amber stays with caution only.
weaknesses: Home's ticker Status segment still says 'Answering · Telegram, Calendar off' rather than '● 6 working'. The home view hands the template no lamp counts (Status counts its models, keys and services rows), so printing 6 would mean hard-coding it. It needs one line in the home view.
Green share is still about 68% on Home and 71% on Chat, above the brief's ~55%. The greeting plate's lit word, tube and Send button carry it, and the chat's Send and her screens carry the rest.
At 390px the Coming up head clears the tab bar, but the first hop row with its lit tube is still just below the fold.
The quote screen keeps about 35px of unlit glass between the Then line and the tape on desktop, and the plate keeps about 50px of ground under the ways to start.
Status's spend register has only one kind of call in the sample data, so it reads as a single line over a gap. It fills properly only with more kinds.
On the To do and Ideas pages the capture's resting pointer leaves one row in its hover wash, which can read as a selection in the still.
The month's '2' (today) still has its live green dot beside it, a second small light on a page whose lit figure is the '4'.
revisions: Law fix: .b-answers .n-on is now clay (--people) with no glow, so Status's only lit figure is the head's '6'. Home's quote-screen '2' is now screen text (phosphor, 1px core and a 12px bloom only, no 34px halo). The lit tape tick's glow was softened, and the hop-tube '4' is Home's single .fig-live.

Home: the quote screen now stands from the eyebrow row to the box's foot (display:contents on .welcome-words, the screen spanning rows 1-2, the starters under both). It is filled with data rather than stretched raster: a larger title and figure and a new 'THEN Fri 9 …' line.

Carried the board's law to Status's lower plates and banks, the Settings index and groups, the To do register (wheat cap), the Ideas register (heather cap) and the new-idea form (heather cap). Each is an unboxed column under a 2px section-ink cap with 1px seams.
Settings: the '0·N' indices are removed from the cards, the side list and the bar's menu. Card heads are label, dotted leader, arrow. Field labels are sentence-case Archivo 500 at 13px.

Month: the next plan's day numeral is the lit figure (VT323 2.1rem, E1), with a 2px phosphor tick on its chip. The head legend reads 'next Sun 4 Oct · 13:00'. Dates drop the leading nought on every page.

Status: deleted the repeated '30-DAY AVERAGE' mono row. The plate's foot is a sentence-case legend ('$1.26 in 30 days, 6 calls', Change the limit), level with the tube's foot, and a dotted-leader register of spend by kind fills the ground between. The ghost and needle were checked: they were already about 55px apart at today's figures, so no offset was needed.

Chat: the change line is set in Plex 500 at 0.9375rem with only '19:53' lit. Vera's older lines are edged in steel instead of 22% green, and her older screens are desaturated, so the chat's green share fell from 74.9% to 70.9%. The family's initials sit on a faint clay tile.
Phone: case padding cut, tape at 2.9rem, Then line hidden, and bottom padding and scroll-padding the height of the tab bar on main and html. Coming up's cap and head now clear the bar.
Typesetting: the Ideas column heads are in sentence case to match To do's, and the hop day numerals are in steel-cyan (a date in its section's ink).

Declined: printing '6 working' in Home's ticker. The home view gives the template no lamp counts, so it would be a hard-coded figure that could go stale, and that would betray a law about figures. It is noted as a one-line change in the view.

Declined in part: 'do not stretch the case'. I let the screen span the speaker and box rows, but only after filling its glass with real data (the Then line, a larger title and figure). The leftover glass above the tape is about 35px, not the 150px the 14a lesson warns about.
crit: The law is broken on its own Status page, and Home has three lights where it should have one. In sheet.css, `.b-answers .n-on { color: var(--brand) }` prints the Answers count '3' in bright phosphor. It is a count, so it should be ink: give it --people, or --heading with a bone figure, so that the head's '6' is the page's only lit figure. On Home, the quote screen's '2' (.qs-fig at 5.25rem with a 34px bloom), the lit tape tick and the hop-tube '4' all glow, and they all quote the same plan. Either the hop-tube '4' is the page's single .fig-live and the screen's '2' is set as screen text (the --phosphor-dim strength, the 12px bloom only, nothing at 34px), or the screen keeps the light and Coming up's first row loses the date line the tube already gives, so the plan is not printed twice. The tube's '2' currently outshines the figure the brief names as the live one.

Home, .welcome / .quote-screen: the tube sits about 190px down the right column with empty cobalt plate above it, and the page's most important light ends up below the title's sight line. Do not stretch the case (the 14a lesson). Set `.welcome { align-items: start }` and give the screen `align-self: start` with its top on the eyebrow row ('Vera | FRIDAY 2 OCTOBER'), so the NEXT UP tag lines up with the date and the plate's height comes from the ask column. If glass is left at the tube's foot, fill it with data: the next plan's place or weather line (.next-where), not a taller tape.

The board's law stops at Home. Settings (.settings-index cards), General's plates, Status's three lower plates (Who answers / Keys / Connected to), the To do table and the form are still rounded, filled boxes. Carry the system onto them. Status's lower plates and the Settings index become typeset columns under a 2px cap in the section's ink with 1px --rule seams, as on Home. name: Dessau, Dialled
tagline: A Bauhaus poster over a working body: each page's name set large beside a square of its ink, one round green tube drawing that page's own data (a 28-day dial on Home, a leaf on Plans, a meter on Status, nine parts on Settings), and rows in the poster's four shapes.
concept: The line keeps its Bauhaus poster: a big sentence-case name, a square of section ink, one green primary and one round phosphor tube. Every circle now draws real data and nothing else. Home has a true 28-day dial whose rim is lit only from now to the next plan. Plans has a calendar leaf, Status a square-root meter, To do an amber LATE, Ideas a numbered map and Settings nine segments, one per part. Around the tubes the page is a calm, matte printed poster in section inks, wheat figures and clay for the family, and the only light is the machine reporting.
companions: Steel-cyan #86b4ba (Plans) is on the head squares, the 4px column caps at 75%, the strip labels, the head link 'All plans', the starter key's square and, new, the dial's waypoint rings that are not next (a matte plans ink on the glass, so only the next ring is green). Denim #90a8cc (To do) and heather, now lifted to #a88ad0 (Ideas), take the same places: caps, squares, labels, head links, the Ideas row numerals and the form's margin rule. Wheat #dcc58f is for every strip figure, the day numeral in Coming up's date line ('SUN 4 OCT') and the meter's written figures. Bone #e6e0d4 at 88% sets the poster and TODAY. Clay #c58b6b marks restaurants and the Family/Memory squares, and #bf9d80 caps the family's chat bubbles. Pewter #5d6469 is now the ask box's border at rest, the dial's grid, track and day ticks, the dashed run, past days' rings in the month, off lamps and the meter's track (#7d868c); #9aa5ae marks the dial's week ticks and labels and the Settings/Status squares. Steel #7f93a3 is the setup bar and its first step, Settings' eight lit segments and the strip's needs-a-look square. Amber is late only: the LATE cell, late rows, the meter's limit tick, the To do tube's 3 and the 'Needs a look' words. Kinds: activity wheat #cdb27a, restaurant clay, outing sage #8fc29b, trip steel #86a9c9, show brick-rose #c4898f, day trip pewter-teal #859f99, and seasonal moved to an olive #a8a86c. A warm stone #cfc6b4 replaces the blue-grey accent of the pages that have no colour of their own.
decisions: Revised in place from the first draft. Palette: palettes/x14b-dessau-cross.json. Variant: variants/x14b-dessau-cross/ (sheet.css; templates home, _ask, _ui, base, ideas, idea_form (new), plans, plans_month, settings, status, tasks). removed.txt is empty.

Week ticks cross the rim at 90/180/270, and their 1w/2w/3w labels sit inside, between the hub and the ring band, at about 18px VT323 in pewter-ink. name: Plate, Channelled
tagline: A matte slate plate over one lit screen, its cuts carrying their light down engraved channels to the rows they report, lit only from now to next.
concept: This is Plate, Engraved with its light carried into the lists. The page is one matte slate plate over a live phosphor screen, and light shows only where the plate is cut. Each cut's shape says what it shows: slot = time, round = range, square = Vera, pinhole = lamp. One new cut, the channel, is a 2px groove that carries a cut's light to the row it reports, lit only from now to the next thing. Coming up's light now drops straight from the slot's Now edge to Next's node. To do's late stretch carries amber and meets a lit NOW crossing. Status's round dial feeds a groove over the lamps that work. It feels calm and machined, and the light visibly goes somewhere and lands.
companions:
- Slate (#13181b) is the plate and graphite (#192024) its keys.
- Steel (#6b8396, cap #9cc4dc) is structure: the seams, the starters' one edge (now the cap, so it reads), the month's 'here' ring, the chip edges (35% plans toward steel), the Ideas head icon and the focused field's outline.
- Brass (#ad9b78) is every engraved word: plain-word placards, the starters' 'lands in' lines (now set above the words), lamp names and the model in the foot.
- Bone (#d4cfc4) is reading text and linen (#ebe6da) is headings. Denim (#9db6d6) is links.
- Amber (#f7b955) has two jobs only. Late: the late stretch of To do's channel, 'was due' and the 3 LATE tag; the checkbox outlines are no longer amber. 'Needs a look': the setup lead rule, the Status tally, and on Settings the amber channel into that part's arrow.
- Each kind's ink sits in a 22px square cut whose floor is that ink mixed 70% toward slate: activity lemon, restaurant orange, outing sage, trip cyan and wishes pink, with no glow.
- Bright #6dff9c stays only in the cuts and lit states: the stencil 'plan', Send, focus and the focused field's top lip, the live pinholes (now on every Settings part that works), the NOW lamp, Next's tick, node and drop, the dial's needle and hub, the lit stretches of channel and the glass.
decisions: THE CHANNEL is written once: tokens on :root plus .channel, .channel.lit and .channel.h. The groove is ::before, a 1px #05080a shadow with a 1px #2a3339 lip. The light is ::after, 55% #6dff9c with a 4px and 12px halo at .35. Lists use the same tokens on their own pseudo-elements, because an <ol> cannot hold a span.

COMING UP: the light runs in one straight line. The channel_bus macro now draws a single lit drop from the slot's Now edge (x = 7px + 1.6rem) through the lower bevel. The rows' channel sits at that same x, and the rows are indented 14px past it, so the list hangs from Now. The groove is lit from the top down to Next's node and unlit after it. The other ticks have no wires: hovering or focusing a row lights its own tick in the slot (generated :has() rules). Nodes have a visible #3a464e ring, so the unlit ones read. Plans' list view uses the same rules.

TO DO (Sill Line's rail as a channel through the checkbox column): amber at dim strength through the late rows, a horizontal lit NOW crossing with a 7px square pinhole lamp breathing (E20), and an unlit groove after it. '#4' follows the title in faint 13px mono, and 'was due' sits on the title's left edge.

STATUS: the spend is a ROUND cut, 13rem across. It is a 240-degree square-root dial in inline SVG (angle = -120 + 240*sqrt(v/max), drawn with rotate() because Jinja has no trigonometry). It has an amber limit tick, a dashed ghost needle at the busiest of the 30 days, a live needle with its glow, and a pinhole hub. The dial drops a lit channel onto a groove along the top of the lamp strip. The groove is lit only over the lamps that work, and every lamp's stub hangs from it. Bank names now sit under their lamps, so the groove runs clear. The tally steps a 30px linen 600 figure against a 13px label-ink unit.

THE MONTH: each day with a plan is a 28px window holding its VT323 numeral at about 74% phosphor, readable at a squint. Today is at full strength with E1's halo and the steel ring. The per-plan pulse dash is gone. Each event is a 44px target with a steel edge tinted 35% toward plans.

GREETING: 'What should Vera *plan*?' is set at 44px condensed linen, with only E1's halo on 'plan'. E7's edgeless scanlined pool falls on the box's top lip, now at .16 alpha. The starters are three plate keys flush to the box's foot with 1px seams and a steel-cap edge, and 'lands in ...' is engraved above the words. The three brass lines share one baseline even when a key wraps.

NEXT UP: the words sit in a fixed left track, with an 8.5rem track kept for the round radar. Only the name is at full strength. The date, [IN 2 DAYS], the facts ('for Maya, Theo · Activity') and '› 3 more on the slot' are on the E15 dim tier. NEXT UP is dim glyphs over a 1px phosphor rule instead of a solid fill. The radar's ring labels are gone, and the placard was dropped earlier.

SETTINGS gets its lamp. Each part's status line hangs a pinhole in the gutter: lit when the part is working, an unlit cut when its line says off, not set up or not connected. The part that needs a look keeps its amber pin, and its dotted leader becomes an amber channel into the arrow. Sign-in stays in the two-column flow, and the keys are square.
FORM: a focused field is lit along its top lip only (E4 kept to the cut edge) and outlined in steel cap. The halo all round is gone.

PHONE: the starters are one row of three compact keys at 13px. Next up drops the radar track, so the name sets on one line, and the radar shrinks to 5.5rem over the bezel's corner. Next up is now in view above the tab bar.

BUDGET: build.py now also strips spaces round braces, semicolons, commas and colons in the design's own rules (none of them holds a string with those characters). The sheet is 187,892 characters, with the readable plate.css, cross.css and channel.css beside it.

name: Trued, Yard Lit
tagline: The family's week as a signal box's lit track diagram: the Next up tube as the line's lit headlamp, plates hung on leaders over their stops, every section opened on a steel siding, a yard of the house's other rooms, and one lamp at the foot of every page.
concept: Trued's idea stays: the family's week drawn as a signal box's lit track diagram, with a terminus, ring stops, a T buffer and one lamp at now. The boxes go. Only the greeting board and the tubes keep a frame, so Ideas' filters and the New idea form now sit on the ground too. Every other section opens on a rule head drawn as a siding and is parted from the next by an engraved seam. Plates hang on leaders above their stops and carry a second fact, the drive from home. The house's other rooms form one dense siding yard, which now also holds setup. Every page ends on the line's last signal, a lamp that lights only while a turn is being answered. It should feel like one signal box diagram at night, lit only where the line is live.
companions: Steel #9cc3dd is the wiring. It takes the rule heads' terminus bars and buffers, the 1px #2e343b rules and the rails (now #566a80), the yard's ring stops and icons, and links (steel, underlined only on hover). It also takes the plates' route marks and drive bearings, the box's edge at rest (42% steel) and the foot's ring at rest. Cyan #74e6f0 goes with plans: the ring stops on Coming up's rail, a plate's kind word at 80%, the ring before a plan day's numeral on the month, and the date chips' month. Sage #86d9a6 is 'Now' beside the lit tick on To do, 'Answering' in the foot, and the afterglow's edge. Amber is used only for late words, the 'Late 3' key's words and the half lamps ('needs a look'), never for an outline or a ring. Graphite #15191a with a #2c3336 hairline is a plan's plate. #6dff9c stays on the motif list: the mark, Send, 'plan.' (E1 with a hot core), the box while someone types, the tubes' glass, the now lamps and the lit run, the power wires (the tube's and the phone readout's), the yard's next setup stop, the foot's lamp while a turn runs, and focus.
decisions: Title: 'Tell Vera what to *plan.*', as the 14a lessons asked for Trued. It is an instruction rather than a question, since the question forms are retired. It sits on one line on desktop with 'plan' and its full stop inside the lit run (E1 with a hot core: 0 0 2px #eafff1, 0 0 8px brand/.75, 0 0 22px brand/.38). On a phone 'what to plan.' is held together with nowrap, so it breaks as 'Tell Vera / what to plan.' with no orphan.

Coming up is de-nested. The slate band is gone, the section opens on a rule head beside the tube, and the rail is its floor. I bent the brief here: each plate hangs under the head at its content height, and its 1px leader grows down to its stop. The spare height reads as track, not as graphite or empty ground.

Each plate has three parts. First, the kind ring and kind word (cyan at 80%). Second, the name at 19px Archivo 700, 88% width, balanced, two lines at most, through the nb binding. Third, a foot with the sunk mono time well and whom, then the drive from home. The drive sits behind the line's own route mark (the terminus bar on its side, 10px of steel) and is set like the Ideas Drive column: tabular DM Mono, figures at ink weight, 'h' and 'min' in ink-2, and the direction in steel ('2 h 05 min NE'). It is left out when unknown. The last plate's right edge now meets the rail's buffer.

Rule heads on every page's section heads: Home, Status, Settings groups, Plans month and list, and Ideas' new 'Find'. Each has a 2x12px steel terminus, the name at the 24px step in Archivo 600 94%, the count in DM Sans, a 1px #2e343b rule and a T buffer. A head with a link ends at it: the link sits right against the buffer with no stub between, in steel and not underlined at rest. On a phone the head is a two-row grid. Row 1 holds the terminus, name, rule, link and buffer; row 2 holds the count, under the name and starting at its left edge.

Engraved seams (1px #20272b over a 3% white highlight) part the sections. Frames are gone from To do, Lately added, the Status panels, the Settings cards and groups, the month and To do trays, and now also Ideas' filter bar and the New idea form.

The siding yard, 'Around the house', is one steel line under both columns. It has a ring stop for Wishes (each kid a link with her open count), Memory (how many things she keeps, from the memories table), Family (people) and Settings. Under each ring are its steel icon, its name and its state on one baseline, with counts in tabular DM Mono ink-2. The whole stop is the target: its link covers the stop, and the inner links sit above it. Names underline only on hover or focus. Stops sit at their natural width 2rem apart, and the line runs on to its buffer. I kept the yard under both columns because a right-column yard would leave a hole on the left.

Setup is folded into the yard. While steps are left, the Settings stop is the yard's one lamp: its ring is lit #6dff9c with a hot core and reads '3 to finish · Choose your own password', with the next step as a link. When nothing is left it is a steel ring, or an amber half lamp while something needs a look. The separate 'Finish setting up' strip and its seam are deleted.

The status foot is on every page but sign-in. Under a seam, the lamp, its word, 'OpenAI gpt-6-luna' (model in DM Mono) and '$0.00 of $2.00 today' (tabular DM Mono) sit at their natural widths on fixed 2.5rem steel leaders. One rule then runs to 'Status →' at a T buffer. The lamp is lit #6dff9c and breathing, with the word 'Answering', only while a message is held under a live claim, that is, while a turn is being worked on. At rest it is a steel ring with 'Ready'. It is an amber half lamp with the status words when something needs a look, and a dashed ring when it cannot answer.

Phone: a one-line glass readout under the box (NEXT, the plan's name lit, its day and time) links to the plan. A 2px lit power wire runs from it into the starter branch's junction. The starter rings stay dark at rest, and the month strip is kept as a 4px trace.

Ideas: the filters sit on the ground under a 'Find' rule head with a seam under them. The New idea form is unboxed, and its ring-stop field rail is the floor, with rings labelled by their fields. The seam over Add it / Cancel starts at the fields' edge, so the rail runs on unbroken to its T buffer.
Plans month: Earlier, This month and Later are steel text links inside the head row, before the buffer, so the rule runs unbroken to them.

Settings: the sticky save bar has a solid surface fill, an engraved-seam top edge and a shadow of page ground above it, and the last group has 2.5rem of margin below it. Nothing passes underneath, and the empty 'changed' slot no longer breaks a folded group's rule.
To do: margin dates in one line of 12px DM Mono, 'Now' in 13px sage DM Sans 600, the 'Late 3' key in amber words in a steel frame, and square ticks. All unchanged.
Status: the case and the lamp well share one height, the tally sits at the head of the well, and the working lamps breathe. Unchanged apart from the rule-head link fix.

Colour: the rail token moved from #58697a to #566a80, slightly bluer steel, so every rail reads as the steel wiring it is. Together with steel and cyan taking the removed fills' share, this puts Home at 59.8% green.

crit: Home, Around the house (.yard / .yard-line / .ys): it is the sparsest thing on the page. Four stops are spread across 1120px with about 270px of bare steel between them. Put the name and its count on one baseline (.ys-name then .ys-say inline, the count in tabular DM Mono ink-2, drop text-decoration at rest and underline only on :hover/:focus-visible). It should feel like one signal box diagram at night rather than a dashboard of cards, lit only where the line is live.

name: Lit Manual, Dialled
tagline: The family's operator manual, dialled: the round countdown tube carries the plan days on its ticks, one lit leader drops from it onto NOW, and the same engraved day numeral marks the dial, the rails and the month.
concept: The page is still the family's operator manual, set in Plex in bone on green-black. Every dated list hangs from an unboxed drawing-ink rail with one NOW. Its bezel prints 28 day ticks, a lamp on each plan's day with that day's numeral upright on the glass, and the free weekend as a sage arc. On Home, one straight lit leader drops from the tube's socket into Coming up's NOW lamp. It is now the only lit stroke on the page, because every NOW rule across a list has been dimmed to a fading 1px trace. The light sits where the machine is live, and the rest of the page is a calm, grounded manual.
companions: Bone ink (#dcd8ca) carries text, the engraved numerals and the head counts on every page; the counts are now all bone. Drawing-ink slate (#6f88b3 / #9fb4d6) carries rails, readout leaders and stops, and the drive times on Ideas. Every rail stop on To do is now a slate square, including the late ones. name: Waypoint, Patched

The Next up tube sits in Coming up's right column, and one short, straight phosphor patch lead joins it to the Next row it reports. One rule holds on every page: the filled jewel means Now or today, and Next is always the lit ring. Light runs only along the path from Now to Next; the rest is bone, steel and slate, calm and exact, and every hover is a steel afterglow.

firstDraft.name: Waypoint, Patched
firstDraft.concept: This is Waypoint, Ruled with each of its judged holes filled by something real, and the 1969 instrument left whole. The Next up tube moves into Coming up's empty right column at a larger size, and one short, straight phosphor patch lead runs from the Next row into a steel socket on the tube's case. That lead wires the light to the row it reports. Light runs only along the path from Now to Next. The rest of the page is bone, steel and slate, calm and exact.
